thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PD-7261 fired — p99 latency breach in eu-west-1 for /v1/generate. p99 = 1320ms (SLO 500ms). alert rule: latency-p99 > 1000ms for 2m. dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/latency/eu-west-1

sara-oncall: acked. I'm on rotation. assigning to Alex (sre) for investigation.

alex-sre: I'm booting up tracing, grabbing spans now. do we have a recent config/rollout in eu-west?

liam-eng: no config rollouts in last 30m. seeing sudden spike in request queue length on pods behind gateway-eu-1, KV cache evictions up ~3x.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation: PD escalation to L2 after 3 minutes (auto). Notifying oncall-l2.

nina-support: quick check on customer impact — our support dashboard shows 12 active customers with increased error latency, 2 accounts reporting timeouts in last 5m. opening a ticket for those customers.

alex-sre: plan: 1) divert traffic to eu-dedicated-warm pool (fallback). 2) bump autoscaler target for inferencer job in eu-west by +30% to drain queues. 3) temporary KV cache prewarm/pin for hot prefixes. 4) if no improvement in 5m, rollback recent model quantization toggle (if active).

sara-oncall: doing step 1 now — adding route rule to prefer eu-dedicated-warm for /v1/generate. will report back. (will run manual canary) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

ops-bot: runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.internal/latency-p99-response – recommended checks: autoscaler, kvcache-evictions, hotkey list, recent deployments.

alex-sre: running quick check on autoscaler metrics. current desired=40, actual pods=38. queue length per pod ~85 (target <30).

liam-eng: logs show repeated 503s from sidecar pool on node euw-3, and kernel: "throttle: nvenc saturation" entries — looks like a hot path on GPU sidecar causing backpressure.

sara-oncall: updating PD incident with initial customer impact and mitigation steps. PD note: "diverting to dedicated pool, bumping autoscaler".

alex-sre: performing autoscaler bump now — running:

```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood.internal/autoscaler/eu-inferencers/scale -d '{"desired":52}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OP_TOKEN'
```
If approved, this should add ~14 pods (30%).

liam-eng: while that's scaling, can someone trigger KV warmup for top prefixes? i'll paste list: user:, session:, prompt:sys: — prefetch script below.
```
./tools/warm_kv.sh --region eu-west-1 --keys-file /tmp/hotkeys.txt
```

nina-support: sending support msg to the two affected customers with interim mitigation notes. no external outage notice yet.

incident-bot: PD-7261 updated: "Autoscaler bumped, traffic diversion initiated, KV prewarm triggered." Current p99: 980ms (was 1320ms). trending downward.

sara-oncall: seeing improvement on dashboard — p99 dropped to ~700ms after traffic diversion, still above SLO but better. continuing mitigation. tagging alex as primary for stabilization. handing off primary ownership.

alex-sre: will keep monitoring. next steps if not back to normal in 10m: remove any queued large-batch jobs, temporarily disable long-tail batching at gateway, and if necessary rotate traffic regionally.

liam-eng: removed a large batch job from queue; also deployed a small patch to reduce max-batch-size from 256 -> 128 on canary.

pagerduty-bot: Note: PD incident will escalate to SEV-1 if customer errors > 5% across top 20 customers. Monitor error-rate.

ops-bot: checklist update: autoscaler bumped, kvcache warmup run, route diversion applied, large-batches canceled.

alex-sre: p99 now at 460ms, within SLO. leaving a 30m watch. updating PD-7261: mitigated, root cause suspected GPU-sidecar saturation + sudden batch-jam. next: post-incident triage and retrospective.

sara-oncall: thanks team. handing off to oncall-l2 for night watch — alex will be primary. I'll close my ack once PD updated. :white_check_mark:

nina-support: filing customer followups and summary for impacted accounts.

incident-bot: PD-7261 status: mitigated -> monitoring. closing ephemeral channel in 30m if stable.

sara-oncall: final note before stepping out — document the temporary config changes (autoscaler desired back to previous value later) and flag for postmortem.

alex-sre: noted. I'll snapshot cluster state and collect traces. handing off.

sara-oncall: handoff complete. good job everyone. :clap:
